title: Reviewer Conflict of Interest in Grant Panels
bottleneck: Peer reviewers are drawn from the same small expert pools as applicants, creating direct competition: a reviewer may soon apply for the same pot of money. Studies and insider accounts describe reviewers discounting innovative proposals that threaten their own research programs, with anonymity shielding the behavior. Double-blind review of grants is rare, and in small fields true anonymity is nearly impossible to maintain.
why_it_blocks: Competitor-review corrupts merit allocation and teaches applicants to propose only what incumbents find unthreatening. The bias is invisible in any single decision, emerging only in the portfolio of funded work.
current_state: Conflict-of-interest rules exist but are weakly enforced; proposals for blinded or non-competitor review remain pilot-scale. Structural fixes like lottery-among-qualified proposals would sidestep the problem but face institutional resistance.

sources.title: Evidence and the Design and Reform of Scientific Institutions (Nintil)
